source_review.notes: Checked all 12 structured references against current official NIST, EU, UK ICO, Apache Iceberg, Google Cloud, AWS, PostgreSQL, and Cloud Security Alliance sources. Verified the September 2025 NIST media-sanitization revision, lifecycle/privacy framing, snapshot/branch/orphan maintenance behavior, BigQuery time-travel and fail-safe semantics, S3 versioning/lifecycle/object-lock behavior, MVCC vacuum context, and current storage-limitation guidance in their stated scopes; every final URL returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked notation for objects, scope-graph nodes, policy revisions, trigger time, minimum/maximum durations and boundaries, holds, eligibility, node outcomes, completion and coverage.
Checked tuple, predicate, quantified-set, equivalence, conjunction, negation, cardinality and ordering syntax for defined symbols and balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates temporal policy eligibility, layer-specific disposition outcomes, declared graph scope and completed-versus-excepted states.

evidence: Executed retention-eligibility-states and matched one delete, one active hold, one not-due, one dependency-blocked and one unknown-policy record plus true full accounting exactly.
Recomputed exercise boundaries from closure day 40: minimum day 70 and maximum day 100, with the day-105 active hold correctly blocking deletion.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic fixture partitions all five records into mutually exclusive lifecycle states and preserves unknown evidence rather than permitting deletion.

evidence: Expanded eligibility and confirmed known evidence, passage of binding boundaries and absence of active hold are necessary in the stated deletion-requiring model.
Verified completion quantifies over every declared required node and permits only deleted, approved-anonymized, expired, or explicit documented-exception outcomes.
Verified safety and liveness proof sketches depend respectively on current hold/policy binding and eventual scope/executor/retry plus finite hold/exception assumptions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Formal claims do not equate one database flag, exception, anonymization label, or unknown denominator with completed deletion.

evidence: Reviewed missing/corrected/late triggers, timezone, conflicting rules, stale hold feeds, hold release, extraordinary volume, unstable selectors, concurrent writes, partial failure, retry and permission drift.

Reviewed MVCC, copy-on-write/delete files, snapshots, branches/tags, in-flight orphan candidates, path mismatch, object delete markers/noncurrent versions, replicas, indexes, caches and garbage collection.

Reviewed immutable backups, restore/replay, resurrection, shared/backup/escrow keys, plaintext copies, crypto-erasure, processors, pseudonyms, aggregates, models, public exports and minimized receipts.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers policy, temporal, identity, storage, concurrency, recovery, cryptographic, downstream, verification and destructive-automation boundaries.

evidence: Traced policy authority/version, stable subject/object identity, trigger/boundaries, holds, graph scope, action, execution, verification, receipts and restore protection through exposition, examples and answers.

Confirmed desired retention, configured lifecycle, effective recoverability, observed access and verified deletion remain distinct at current, historical, replica, cache, export, model, backup and processor layers.
Confirmed tombstones outlive replay paths, restores reapply current state, unknowns remain visible, and receipts minimize content while preserving target/outcome evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: No SQL response, soft delete, catalog removal, snapshot expiration, delete marker, access revocation, key API call, backup catalog entry, processor acknowledgment or job success is described as broader proof than it supplies.

evidence: Reviewed safety derivation from current policy/hold eligibility, stable signed target sets and action-time version guards or re-evaluation.
Reviewed liveness derivation from known finite scope, eventual authorized executor availability, retry/escalation and finite holds/exceptions.
Confirmed missing lineage, stale holds, immutable backup windows and irrecoverable public exports are explicitly identified as assumption failures or bounded constraints.
proof_review.notes: The proof sketches establish conditional executor properties rather than universal legal erasure or physical-media absence.

evidence: Safety and liveness statements are explicitly labeled claims and their arguments proof sketches.
Operational assumptions and real-system counterconditions immediately bound both arguments.
The executable is explicitly labeled policy logic illustration rather than legal interpretation or storage deletion.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Formal model, proof sketch, deterministic policy trace, storage observation, qualified policy decision and legal conclusion remain distinct.

evidence: Current platform and standards behavior is attributed to dated official documentation rather than generalized across all storage systems.

Execution responses, inventories, decision receipts, negative queries, version/reference inspection, key attestations, processor receipts, backup expiry and restore drills are described as layer-specific evidence.
Legal precedence, subject rights, approved anonymization, model disposition and external promises are assigned to qualified authority and scoped context rather than inferred from tooling.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Normative policy, current implementation semantics, mathematical properties, deterministic examples, empirical verification and legal/contract claims are labeled separately.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It integrates temporal policy and conflicts, holds, identity/scope discovery, safe execution, MVCC/lakehouse/object-version semantics, tombstone propagation, recovery, backup immutability, crypto-erasure, media sanitization, derivatives/processors and proof-oriented verification without conflating logical restriction, physical deletion and bounded recoverability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the lifecycle decision record, falsifiable claim, scope inventory, policy/executor separation, target preview, destructive stop conditions, idempotency, storage maintenance, replay/restore gate, backup exception, hold operation, processor workflow, receipt schema, metrics, ten production examples and merger recovery answer for operational usability.
